about: Default export budgets for a mainstream / mid-range gaming PC. Every number carries `src` (ids in `sources`) and a `basis`: 'sourced' (read from a source), 'derived' (worked out from sourced numbers, reasoning in `note`) or 'thin' (little evidence: a conservative pick, revisit). Triangles are rendered triangles. Override any number per export; state the role and target instead of inventing a budget.

target.hardware: mainstream discrete GPU of the RTX 3060 / 4060 / RX 6600-7600 class, 8 GB VRAM, 1080p-1440p, 60 fps (upscaling allowed)
target.console_equivalent: roughly a PS5 / Xbox Series X: current-generation console budgets carry over; PS4-generation budgets are a safe floor
target.note: RTX 3060 / 4060 / 4060 Laptop led the Steam survey most months of 2026 (~3.5-4% each); 8 GB and 16 GB VRAM are each about a quarter of systems, so 8 GB is the conservative memory target.

lod_ratios.note: Unity's Mesh LOD generator halves indices per level; MetaHuman head vertices 24000/12000/6000/2500 (1/0.5/0.25/0.1); MetaHuman body 30500/7600/3350/1507 (below the neck drops faster, and switches half as often: LODSync gives 2 head changes per body change); UE's LOD groups default to 50% and its auto-LOD example uses 75/25/12%.

lod_screen_size.meaning: Unreal-style screen size: projected bounding-sphere diameter / the screen's larger dimension. LOD k is used below screen_size[k] (LOD0 above screen_size[1]).
lod_screen_size.note: No engine documents default character switch sizes. For curved surfaces the triangles a given on-screen error needs grow roughly linearly with the projected size, so halving the triangles at each halving of screen size keeps the error in pixels about constant. Tune with a view-distance test in the target engine; use hysteresis.

hero.what: the player character, seen close up in gameplay and cutscenes

lod0_triangles.note: Hunt: Showdown hunters 35-70k (PC/PS4, 2019); Kratos 80k with 32k face (PS4, 2018); Marius 85k (Xbox One, 2013); Cloud ~220k with hair half of it (PS5, 2024); MetaHuman LOD0 ~100k vertices across head, body and card hair (estimate ~150-200k triangles). Mid-range PC ~ PS5, but 220k is one stylised hero with signature hair: 100k is the conservative middle. 100k -> 103k (2026-10-16, r40): eyes_mouth_lashes was derived from its components (7996, was a thin 5000), and the parts' defaults must fit the total; the sources' spread covers it.

head.note: Kratos face 32k (PS4); MetaHuman head 24k vertices at LOD0 (incl. eyes and mouth interior).

body.note: MetaHuman body 30.5k vertices whole and bare; skin hidden under clothing is removed on export, so a dressed body needs less.

clothing.note: No primary per-garment numbers found. Remainder of the total after head, body and hair; Hunt notes gear drives hero counts up.

hair_cards.note: MetaHuman card hair 30k vertices at LOD0 (+15k facial hair). Cloud's hair was ~110k (half of 220k) as a signature stylised feature; the real cost of cards is overdraw, not triangles.

eyes_mouth_lashes.note: Derived 2026-10-16 (r40, assembly) as the sum of its components' measured needs at hero role, not a sourced figure. eyes 628: both globes + cornea as exported (smallest that stays round in the 1 m close shot). teeth 2828: the upper row whole; it is visible in every smile at 1 m, and decimation was the suspected source of jagged crowns (r20s), so it is not cut. teeth_lower 1400: decimated from 2828 with fewer folds (26 vs 74 folded edges, r39); shown only with the jaw open. tongue 700: 900 -> 700 in v54; no tongue faceting in the 1 m jaw review (x54). lashes 2440: 610 ribbons x 2 segments x 2 triangles (LOD1 already ships that); fewer ribbons changes the eye look (Joe's call). Brows are in the head's texture, none here.

accessories.note: Held hero prop for scale: the Buster Sword is ~8k on PS5.

textures.note: Epic's performance pipeline (UE Optimized) caps MetaHuman maps at 2K; 8K is the cinematic pipeline. Hunt's hero face is 1024 with eyeballs 2048 and hands 4096x2048 (not uniform). Crytek's world target is 512 px/m, hero assets higher. 2048 px/m on the face is ~0.5 mm/texel. Four 2K sets of 3 BC-compressed maps with mips is ~60-70 MB.

materials.note: Skin, eyes, hair, clothing (1-2), accessories. VRChat 'Good' allows 8 slots; Hunt splits hero parts into many materials for customisation.

skeleton.note: Mixamo-compatible body (~65 bones, commonly cited) plus twist bones. MetaHuman uses 12 influences on the head and 8 on the body at LOD0, 4 at far LODs; glTF's single joint set is 4.

face_shapes.note: ARKit's 52 shapes. MetaHuman keeps blendshapes at LOD0 only and body correctives to LOD1: drop morph targets past LOD1.

main_npc.what: a named NPC with dialogue close-ups

lod0_triangles.note: Hunt's bosses 25-45k and non-primary characters 25-35k; VRChat's PC 'Good' cap 70k with many avatars in a room. Close-ups keep the head near hero density; body, clothes and hair are halved.

head.note: Between MetaHuman head LOD0 and LOD1 (24k / 12k vertices).

body.note: About MetaHuman body LOD1 (7.6k vertices) plus hidden-skin removal.

textures.note: Hunt's grunts: 1024 per part (head, hair, upper body, shirt, legs). VRChat 'Excellent' 40 MB.

secondary_npc.what: named-in-passing NPCs: shopkeepers, guards; seen at conversational distance at most

lod0_triangles.note: Below Hunt's non-primary 25-35k because many share the screen; about MetaHuman LOD2 (head 6k + body 3.35k vertices + cards 10k vertices). VRChat 'Excellent' is 32k.

textures.note: One atlas; Crytek's 512 px/m world density.

materials.note: Crytek: combine textures to keep draw calls down; hair usually needs its own alpha-tested material.

lod0_triangles.note: Hunt's far LOD3 4-8k; MetaHuman LOD3 (head 2.5k + body 1.5k vertices; Epic's best LOD on phones); VRChat Quest 7.5-10k. City Sample: only the nearest crowd are full rigs; far ones are vertex-animated static meshes.

hair_cards.note: MetaHuman switches card hair to a hair mesh (500-100 vertices) at its far LODs.

textures.note: Shared atlases across variants; tint per instance.

skeleton.note: Far LODs: vertex-animated static meshes instead of skinning (City Sample).

hair_cards.note: MetaHuman card vertices 30000/15000/10000/3000/1500, then a hair mesh. Hunt's hero hair map is only 512 and grunts 1024; Epic's card generator reserves atlas space so later LODs share the texture. Overdraw: trim cards to their alpha, alpha test (not blend) on desktop, fewer layers at distance, interior cards first to go.

hero_prop.note: A held or inspected prop: the Buster Sword is ~8k on PS5; Hunt's gear maps run 256-2048 by size.

prop.note: 512 px/m is Crytek's world density; size the count by geometric error, not by a number.

tree.note: Leaf cards dominate the count (one anecdote: trunk ~570, leaves 12k+). SpeedTree: LOD settings are the biggest GPU lever, trim interior leaf triangles against overdraw, short draw distance, 3-5 models per species. No primary triangle numbers found.

terrain.note: Unreal's recommended landscape sizes (vertices per side) and its ceiling of 1024 components; each section is a draw call.

metahuman_lod.title: Platform support and LOD specifications for MetaHumans
metahuman_lod.facts: Head vertices 24000/12000/6000/2500/1300/560/270/130; head joints 713->26; blendshapes 669 at LOD0 only; skin influences 12/8/4. Body vertices 30500/7600/3350/1507, correctives LOD0-1. Card hair vertices 30000/15000/10000/3000/1500, hair mesh 500/250/100; facial hair cards 15000/7000/3000/1000/500. PC best LOD 0, max texture 8192; iOS/Android best LOD 3, 2048.

metahuman_textures.title: MetaHuman materials and textures (assembly pipelines)
metahuman_textures.facts: UE Cine assembly bakes normal/specular up to 8K; UE Optimized (performance) caps at 2K.

unity_mesh_lod.title: How the Mesh LOD generator works
unity_mesh_lod.facts: Each LOD has about half the indices of the previous one.

ue_auto_lod.title: Static Mesh automatic LOD generation
ue_auto_lod.facts: LOD groups default to 50% triangles; walkthrough uses 75/25/12%.

ue_skel_lod_api.title: FSkeletalMeshLODGroupSettings::ScreenSize
ue_skel_lod_api.facts: Screen size = projected bounding-sphere diameter (0.5 = half the screen's max dimension); hysteresis only complex->simple. No default values.

ue_cards_lod.title: Creating hair cards and LODs using the hair card generator
ue_cards_lod.facts: Card count / triangle targets per LOD; reserved atlas space so later LODs share the texture.

hunt_budgets.title: Character Budgets (HUNT: Showdown)
hunt_budgets.facts: Hunters LOD0 35-70k, LOD3 5-8k; grunts 25-35k / 4-5k; bosses 25-45k / 4-7k. Hunter maps: face 1024, eyeballs 2048, lashes/hair/beard/brows 512, hands 4096x2048, legs 1024; gear 256-2048. Grunts 1024 per part.

cry_tpm.title: Texels Per Meter
cry_tpm.facts: Most assets ~512 texels/m; hero assets (main characters, cutscene assets) get more; debug presets 256/512/1024.

ps_blog_2019.title: The polygonal evolution of 5 iconic PlayStation characters
ps_blog_2019.facts: Kratos (God of War 2018) 80,000 polygons, 32,000 in the face, 140+ textures; Kazuya (Tekken 7) head 2,800, 6,000 with hair and mouth.

ff7_rebirth.title: Final Fantasy VII Rebirth: the polygonal evolution
ff7_rebirth.facts: Cloud ~110k (Remake, PS4) -> ~220k (Rebirth, PS5); hair about half the model; Red XIII ~120k (card fur); Buster Sword ~8k.

ryse_dice.title: Crytek on Ryse (DICE talk coverage) / Making-of Ryse
ryse_dice.facts: Marius 85,000 triangles, 770 joints (500+ deforming, 260 facial), 230 corrective face blendshapes, 8 skin influences.

vrchat_ranks.title: Avatar Performance Ranking System
vrchat_ranks.facts: PC Excellent/Good: 32k/70k triangles, 40/75 MB textures, 4/8 materials, 75/150 bones. Quest 7.5k/10k/15k/20k.

city_sample.title: City Sample project
city_sample.facts: Nearest crowd characters are full MetaHumans; farther ones vertex-animated static meshes; hundreds on screen. No triangle numbers.

steam_survey_2026.title: Steam Hardware Survey coverage, March-September 2026
steam_survey_2026.facts: RTX 3060 / 4060 / 4060 Laptop top most months at ~3.5-4%; RTX 5070 led September; 16 GB VRAM 25.9% vs 8 GB 25.3% (July).

df_ps5_gpu.title: Digital Foundry PS5 vs PC GPU comparisons
df_ps5_gpu.facts: PS5 GPU lands between an RTX 2070 Super and 2080 Super / RTX 3060 Ti in Valhalla; i.e. about today's mainstream PC GPU.

speedtree_gpu.title: SpeedTree Runtime SDK: GPU performance
speedtree_gpu.facts: LOD is the biggest frame-rate lever; trim interior leaf triangles (overdraw); short draw distance; 3-5 models per species.

speedtree_lod.title: SpeedTree Runtime SDK: level of detail

polycount_tree.title: Polycount thread on tree triangle counts
polycount_tree.facts: Trunk and main branches ~570 triangles; leaves push past 12k.

ue_landscape.title: Landscape technical guide
ue_landscape.facts: Recommended sizes 127..8129 vertices per side; max 1024 components; each section a draw call.
